Notes: 1. Threshold: minimum physical pixel displacement required to trigger a gesture. 2. Resistance: movement ratio after triggering. Higher resistance makes the map respond more slowly and steadily.
Default 2.0 zooms in 1 level, 4.0 zooms in 2 levels. Minimum 1.1, maximum 5.0.

Note: Repeated double taps can interrupt an ongoing zoom, so observed zoom changes may be lower than the theoretical cumulative amount. For validation, use a single double tap and wait for the animation to settle.
Matches CameraPosition.bearing (0-360°, clockwise from north). Min 0° and max 360° means unrestricted. Other ranges limit two-finger rotation and rotate inertia.

When custom detection is enabled, two taps within the delay are treated as double-tap zoom. Try 300-500ms.
gesture-center zooms around the gesture point (e.g. two-finger midpoint or double-tap point); screen-center zooms around the screen center.
Controls whether gestures produce fling inertia after release. Duration is a base gesture parameter; 0 also disables inertia. The current duration is saved when disabled.
Sets zoom transition duration for double-tap, two-finger tap, etc. 0 ms means instant. Disabling restores the default 300 ms.

This mode owns the map; overlays do not stack with other modes.
PolyUtil.locationIndexOnEdgeOrPath returns the segment index hit by the query point. closed=true treats the last→first edge as a segment.
PolyUtil.distanceToLine returns the shortest geodesic distance from the test point to the finite segment S–E (meters).
PolyUtil.isClosedPolygon is true only when there are ≥2 points and the first and last coordinates are exactly equal (no tolerance).
